key_insight: Language-only models can partially perform viewpoint-rotation reasoning without visual inputs, and interpretability analyses reveal which internal components and linguistic cues enable this capability.
problem_solved: Determines whether and how models reason about 3D viewpoint changes when only given text (no images), clarifying the limits and mechanisms of spatial intelligence in LLMs versus VLMs.
method: Construct a text-only benchmark of viewpoint-rotation tasks and contrast performance of LLMs and VLMs given identical linguistic descriptions.

Use interpretability tools (probing classifiers, attention and activation analysis, interventions) to identify representations, attention patterns, and neurons correlated with viewpoint transformations.
Ablation and controlled prompt experiments to test which linguistic cues and model components are necessary or sufficient for correct rotation reasoning.
impact: Helps practitioners understand when language models can substitute for vision in spatial tasks, guiding design of multimodal systems, benchmarks, and targeted interventions to improve spatial reasoning or avoid failure modes.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing: text prompt → LLM / VLM branch → task output, with interpretability probes attached
Bar chart comparing accuracy on the text-only viewpoint benchmark across model families
Heatmaps of attention/activation highlighting components implicated in rotation reasoning
Examples panel: side-by-side input prompt, model prediction, and human-annotated ground truth
paper_title: How Do LLMs and VLMs Understand Viewpoint Rotation Without Vision? An Interpretability Study
paper_authors: Zhen Yang, Ping Jian, Zhongbin Guo, Zuming Zhang, Chengzhi Li
